# Dino Atlas Recursive Expansion Queue

## Fixed Loop

1. Pick the next taxon from an already represented clade or ecosystem neighbor.
2. Add one representative full-body image, one same-body color/pattern variant, and one ecology/reference scene.
3. Register the taxon in `app.js` with gallery entries, identity checklist, visual variation profile, and generation route guide.
4. Verify `app.js` syntax, declared asset paths, catalog card image, detail gallery, review lightbox category scope, and phylogeny overlap on desktop/mobile.
5. Promote only count-level candidates; keep ecology and multi-animal scenes as review/reference until anatomy is checked.

## Style Diversity Rule

- Avoid repeating the same side-on floodplain chase composition. Rotate between low ground-level views, over-shoulder prey views, oblique three-quarter herd views, tight-but-full-body defensive contact views, waterline/reflection views, dusk or overcast lighting, forest-edge screens, trackway foregrounds, and elevated slope views while keeping feet and tails readable.
- Avoid reusing the same olive/blue-gray/copper/speckle recipe across taxa. Introduce deliberate species-specific palettes and pattern structures such as countershaded charcoal with pale ocelli, rust mask with broken flank bars, teal throat patch with cream dorsal pinstripes, red-bed dusted ochre with dark chevrons, pale shoulder saddle with peppered neck spots, muted violet-gray shadow bands, or high-contrast juvenile/adult pattern differences when plausible.
- When adding color/pattern variants, describe the palette and pattern as a first-class visible cue, not just a prompt afterthought, and keep the variant below the representative unless anatomy is fully audited.
- When adding ecology scenes, vary camera angle, distance, weather, time of day, terrain, foreground elements, and interaction beat before repeating another broadside pursuit.
- When adding ankylosaurian predator scenes, do not show predators biting, peeling, or tearing through the hard dorsal armor plates or back scutes. Plausible attack or scavenging access should use limbs, lower neck, lower flank, or exposed softer belly-side access; otherwise use defensive bracing, tail-club strikes, or standoff behavior.

## Reusable Output Contract

For each added taxon, produce:

- `assets/dinosaurs/{id}-...-imagegen-v1.png` files.
- `dinosaurs[]` entry.
- `generatedImageSamples[id]` entries.
- `identityChecklists[id]` entry.
- `visualVariationProfiles[id]` entry.
- `generationRouteGuides[id]` entry.
- Verification notes with syntax, asset paths, card render, gallery count, review lightbox category count, and phylogeny overlap count.
